styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Museums, the Rosicrucian Egyptian Museum and the old downtown.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Farm-to-table dining, taquerias and the Japantown bakeries.

styles.label: Nature
styles.blurb: Alum Rock trails, the Guadalupe River path and nearby hills.

stays.why: Walk to museums, the convention center and the San Pedro Square food spots. Best base without a car.
Gallery and nightlife quarter south of downtown; close to the convention center and the arts scene.
Shops, restaurants and a lively evening scene; good for couples and shoppers, but you'll want a car or ride app.
Quiet, walkable and full of Japanese restaurants and markets; a short ride from downtown.

food: Try a Mission-style burrito or a plate of tacos at a taqueria; many are cheap and filling, roughly $10–15.
San Pedro Square Market downtown: many small stalls under one roof, good for groups and picky eaters.
Japantown for ramen, sushi and Japanese bakeries; walk the few blocks and pick what looks busy.
The area grows much of the region's produce; look for farm-to-table menus and weekend farmers' markets.
Book popular dinner spots ahead for Friday and Saturday; walk-ins can mean a long wait.
more_time: Add a day for the Rosicrucian Egyptian Museum and the rose garden next door; a calm, cheap half-day.
Nature lovers: swap an afternoon for a hike at Alum Rock Park in the eastern hills; go early in summer.
Have a car? Drive to the coast (Santa Cruz) or the hills for a half-day; check traffic before you go.

recommend.why: Two nights covers downtown museums, the food markets and a half-day outdoors; add a night if you want a coast or hill trip.

month_notes: January: cool and wet, highs near 15°C. Pack a rain jacket and layers.
February: similar to January, around 17°C highs; a few dry days for walking.
March: still showery (about 10 rain days) but warming to 18°C.
April: drier and milder, highs near 20°C. Good month for walking and parks.
May: mostly dry and pleasant, highs around 23°C. Great for outdoors.
June: dry and warm, highs near 28°C. Start hikes early; afternoons get hot.
July: hot and dry, highs near 29°C. Plan indoor sights at midday.
August: as hot as July, around 29°C, and dry. Carry water.
September: still warm at 28°C but rain returns (about 1 day).
October: cooling to 25°C with a few rain days; comfortable for everything.
November: cooler and wetter, highs near 19°C. Bring a jacket.
December: cool and rainy, highs near 15°C. Indoor plans are safest.

climate_guide.summary: Mediterranean-style: mild, wet winters and warm, almost rain-free summers.

items.title: Best time: May to October
items.text: Warm and mostly dry, highs 23–29°C. Ideal for parks, trails and outdoor dining.

items.title: Wet winters
items.text: December to March brings about 9–10 rain days a month. Pack a rain jacket and plan indoor backups.

items.title: Hot summer afternoons
items.text: July and August reach about 29°C. Do hikes and walks in the morning; stay in the shade at midday.

items.title: Cool evenings year-round
items.text: Lows drop to 7–9°C in winter and about 15°C in summer. Bring a light layer for evenings.

items.title: Pleasant shoulder months
items.text: April, May and October are mild and mostly dry — good all-round months to visit.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Layers, a rain jacket for winter, comfortable shoes for walking, and sunscreen and a hat for summer.

transit.best: Walk or ride apps downtown; use light rail and buses for wider trips.

modes.text: No metro. VTA light rail is the closest thing; it links downtown, the airport area and suburbs.
VTA buses cover the city. Pay with a Clipper card or contactless.
Taxis are metered; Uber and Lyft operate widely and are handy for airport and late-night trips.
Driving is easy but downtown parking costs money and rush hour is slow.
Downtown is walkable; bikes and scooters are common for short hops.
VTA light rail links downtown, the airport area and suburbs. Check the day's timetable.
No ferry service in San Jose.
